body:
maya: Heads up — FinCoX (EU) just pushed us for a private deployment next sprint. They require ISO27001 evidence + GDPR DSRs + EU data residency. They also want a custom high-throughput route. Do we fast-track or gate until certification? :thinking:

sam: Quick reality check: private deploy + KMS + region pins I can do in ~2 sprints if we freeze scope. ISO27001 prep and external audit is ~3 months minimum (paperwork + controls + remediation). The throughput bit sounds like config/autoscale and maybe a perf tweak.

leah: Customer is talking about a multi-year contract if we can meet residency and some attestation. They're flexible on timeline if we provide interim safeguards (contractual commitments, restricted scope). I'll ask for a revenue/commitment number but sounds promising. :raised_hands:

oliver: ISO isn't just a stamp — it pulls in identity, patching, infra seg, sigops runbooks, vendor mgmt. We could propose an "ISO-compatible private beta" where we harden configurations and accept a carveout from audit scope for this deployment, but legal will need minimum controls and compensating controls.

sam: To make tradeoffs concrete: propose a minimal carveout plan vs full cert. Quick RICE-ish sketch for prioritization: 
```
Reach = 1 (FinCoX)
Impact = 8 (large ARR if they sign)
Confidence = 60%
Effort = 6 eng-sprints (private + KMS + residency + perf config)
RICE = (1*8*0.6)/6 = 0.8
```
That number is low-ish because Reach=1. If we can show 3 similar prospects, Reach goes up and it looks worth shifting runway.

jin: Also consider sequencing: roll private beta -> restrict external integrations -> sign interim SLA & MSA -> parallelize compliance doc prep. We can deliver something useful earlier without waiting for cert. Sequence reduces risk and helps close the deal earlier.

oliver: Minimum controls I'd expect in an interim carveout: encryption at rest (customer-managed KMS preferred), per-tenant network isolation, centralized audit logs with 90d retention, DSR flow documented, and a signed attestation about restricted features. I'll list these out.

sec-bot: compliance-check: detected gaps relevant to ISO/GDPR: logging retention missing for EU region, KMS integration not enabled for private pools, no documented DSR playbook. Estimated tasks: 10 infra tickets + 3 policy docs.

leah: Customer asked specifically that we restrict 3rd-party connectors and disable analytics export for their org until we have legal signoff. They said they'd accept it as a temporary limitation.

maya: Proposed decision path: 
1) Sam: give a 2-sprint technical delivery plan for a minimal private deployment (no audit) by EOD.
2) Oliver: share the minimum control list and a short remediation plan for MSA by tomorrow noon.
3) Leah: confirm revenue/commitment and whether customer will accept interim carveouts by EOD.
4) Product: if revenue meets threshold or customer signs a 6+ month interim commitment, green-light sprint bump; else we queue behind ISO program.

sam: I can do the plan — I'll assume no external integrations and standard perf tweaks. Will include risk items.

oliver: Will send control list + suggested compensating controls. Expect a 1-2 page note.

leah: I'll message the customer now and push for written interim acceptance.

maya: Cool. Triage note: this should not become a one-off engineering tax. If we approve, we gate feature flags and create a playbook so we can reuse the pattern. :thumbsup:

jin: Also suggest a follow-up to evaluate "reach" — sales to surface similar prospects. If Reach >= 3, we should reprioritize higher.

sec-bot: audit-log: action items added to compliance board: COMP-421 (KMS for private pools), COMP-422 (DSR playbook), COMP-423 (logging retention).

maya: Thanks everyone — we'll reconvene after the estimates.
